title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BIRDIE'S DOG
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Birdie Lang, a hotel night clerk in Eau Claire, Wisconsin.
She never loses a penny.
Then, one cold November morning, she lost her dog.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: GONE
segments.quote: Look for the helpers. You will always find people who are helping.
segments.author: Fred Rogers
lines: Pickles was a skinny rescue greyhound, scared of everything.
One morning the truck banged, Pickles slipped his collar, and he was gone like a rocket.
Birdie ran down the street in her slippers, alone. Her neighbor Hal stopped her with Mister Rogers' words:
Look for the helpers. You will always find people who are helping.
By noon, forty neighbors were out with flyers. One wore a bathrobe.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: DON'T CHASE
segments.quote: All human evil comes from a single cause, man's inability to sit still in a room.
segments.author: Blaise Pascal
lines: Later, Birdie spotted Pickles behind a gas station. She ran at him. He ran faster.
A lost-dog volunteer named Corinne said, scared dogs run from everyone. Then she quoted Blaise Pascal:
All human evil comes from a single cause, man's inability to sit still in a room.
So Birdie sat still in the park with her stinkiest sweatshirt and a rotisserie chicken.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: NIGHT TWO
segments.quote: If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous he will not bite you. This is the principal difference between a dog and a man.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: On night two, Birdie wondered if Pickles even loved her. He was so new.
Hal read her a line from Mark Twain:
If you pick up a starving dog and make him prosperous he will not bite you. This is the principal difference between a dog and a man.
Pickles knew her smell. She left the porch light on all night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: NIGHT THREE
segments.quote: Hope means hoping when things are hopeless, or it is no virtue at all.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: Night three dropped to twenty-two degrees. Birdie sat shivering, ready to quit.
Corinne handed her cocoa and a line from the English writer G. K. Chesterton:
Hope means hoping when things are hopeless, or it is no virtue at all.
So Birdie stayed. At dawn, a gray nose poked out of the bushes.
Pickles walked right into her lap and ate the chicken.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PROMISE
segments.quote: The fidelity of a dog is a precious gift demanding no less binding moral responsibilities than the friendship of a human being.
segments.author: Konrad Lorenz
lines: At home, she opened a book by Konrad Lorenz, an Austrian animal scientist:
The fidelity of a dog is a precious gift demanding no less binding moral responsibilities than the friendship of a human being.
She bought a harness, a collar he can't slip, and a name tag.
Pickles now wears more safety gear than a hockey goalie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THANK YOU
segments.quote: Gratitude is the fairest blossom which springs from the soul.
segments.author: Henry Ward Beecher
lines: That Sunday, Birdie threw a driveway party for all forty helpers.
The cake said a line from the preacher Henry Ward Beecher:
Gratitude is the fairest blossom which springs from the soul.
Then she joined Corinne's lost-dog team. Last week, she found a beagle.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Ask for help. Sit still. Trust. Keep hoping. Keep your promise. Say thank you.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Ask for help. Sit still. Trust. Keep hoping. Keep your promise. Say thank you.
I once got lost chasing a dog myself. The dog had to walk me home.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
